title: Add multiresolution token attribution and escalation mapper
author: Samir Patel
body: Motivation: teams were seeing noisy token-cost and latency alerts that didn't map cleanly to the specific model stages or invocation cohorts responsible. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a multiresolution token attribution pipeline that produces zoomable rollups (invocation-level, cohort-level, and hour/day rollups) so engineers can quickly slice token cost and latency by prefix/phase/model variant and prompt shape; and 2) an Escalation Mapper service that maps anomaly signals into graded runbooks and escalation channels based on the attribution signature and confidence. Design: the multiresolution pipeline computes lightweight per-invocation 'token signatures' (hashed token-phase histograms + quantized latency percentiles) at ingestion time, then feeds a streaming combiner that emits delta-rollups across three resolutions (invocation, sliding-window cohort, daily bucket) with compact protobuf envelopes. The Escalation Mapper consumes rollups and alert events, performs a small rule-evaluator (yaml driven) and a quick clustering pass (approx k-means on signature vectors) to assign an escalation tier. This enables alerts to target the right on-call rotation (runtime vs model-oncall vs infra) and avoids noisy paging for low-confidence long-tail events. Backwards compatibility: rollups are emitted under a new telemetry topic but existing dashboards and aggregators can opt-in; the mapper publishes enrichment fields to the alert stream and to spans. Implementation details: changes touch the ingestion pipeline (telemetry-producer), the rollup combiner (streaming service), alert enrichment hooks (alert-router), a new grafana dashboard with exploration panels, and a small operator UI for adjusting escalation rules (server-side yaml + validation). Testing and rollout: unit tests for signature computation, integration tests for rollup aggregation, synthetic replay bench to validate no more than 3% added token processing latency at p95. The feature is gated behind a runtime flag and a config toggle per-tenant. Checklist: - [x] Compute token signatures at ingestion - [x] Streaming combiner and proto schema - [x] Escalation mapper rule engine + default rule set - [x] Grafana dashboard + drilldown panels - [x] E2E integration tests and replaybench results - [x] Docs snippet in observability guide - [x] Feature flag and gradual rollout plan Rollout notes: start with internal tenants, enable read-only dashboards, then enable enrichment fields for alerts after 48h of monitoring. If any downstream consumer fails to read the new rollup topic, traffic will fallback to the legacy per-invocation metrics. Related work: ENG-9021 (alert noise reduction), ENG-9150 (token-cost labeling), and the ongoing observability consolidation epic.

files_changed: telemetry/producer/token_signature.proto (new): compact signature envelope for token-phase histograms and p50/p95/p99 latency bins
ingestion/encoder/signature_encoder.go: compute signature at write path, inexpensive hashing and quantization
streaming/combiner/combine_job.py: streaming aggregator that emits invocation, cohort, and daily rollups
alerting/escalation_mapper/service.py: small rule-driven service that assigns escalation_tier and runbook_id
alerting/rules/default_escalation.yaml: default mapping tuned for token-cost spikes, kv-cache misses, and model-variant regressions
dashboards/grafana/multires_token_attrib.json: new dashboard with heatmap, time-zoom, and cohort explorer panels
charts/helm/values-observability.yaml: flag to enable rollups and mapper for a deployment
docs/observability/token-attribution.md: high-level design and runbook mapping guidance
sdk/metrics/README.md: notes on new signature field and consumer migration

reviews: Leah Chen: Great approach. Two asks: include an opt-out header for tenants that cannot produce signatures, and add an alert that fires if rollup lag > 30s. Also prefer configuration-driven bucket boundaries rather than hardcoded ones.
Samir Patel (author): Added opt-out header support and a configuration for bucket boundaries. Rollup lag metric added and dashboard panel shows current lag. PTAL.
Pedro Alvarez: Verified replaybench numbers; p95 ingestion overhead is ~1.8% in our internal tests. Suggest tightening default rule set to avoid escalating low-cardinality KV cache misses.
Maya Thompson: Code-level nits addressed. Suggest using the existing alert-router enrichment API to keep consumers stable. Approving pending CI.
Leah Chen: Reviewed final changes. Approved.

Release notes: Added a multiresolution token attribution pipeline and an Escalation Mapper service to reduce alert noise and route incidents to the correct on-call. Migration: consumers can opt-in to the new rollup topic or continue using existing per-invocation metrics. Backout plan: disable feature flag and revert the rollup topic producer.
